Drug overdose deaths among white men in the United States, 1999-2018

Source: R/data.R
overdose_white_men.Rd

Accidental drug overdose death rates among non-Hispanic and Hispanic white men in the United States by single year of age (15-70) and calendar year (1999-2018), the data shown in Figure 1C/D of Jalal and Burke (2020). overdose_white_men is the age-by-period matrix of rates used by hexamap(); overdose_white_men_long has one row per age and year, with the deaths, population and reliability of each rate.

Usage

overdose_white_men

overdose_white_men_long

Format

overdose_white_men: a numeric matrix with 56 rows (ages 15 to 70) and 20 columns (years 1999 to 2018) of deaths per 100,000 men, with the ages and years as dimnames.

overdose_white_men_long: a data frame with 1,120 rows and 6 columns:

year

Calendar year of death.

age

Age at death, in single years.

deaths

Number of deaths (NA when 9 or fewer).

population

Population of white men of that age, from the bridged-race estimates used by CDC WONDER.

rate

Deaths per 100,000 (NA when deaths are 9 or fewer).

flag

Factor: "reliable" (20 or more deaths), "unreliable" (10 to 19 deaths) or "suppressed" (9 or fewer).

An object of class data.frame with 1120 rows and 6 columns.

Source

Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics. Multiple Cause of Death 1999-2018 on CDC WONDER Online Database, released 2020. Data are from the Multiple Cause of Death Files, 1999-2018, as compiled from data provided by the 57 vital statistics jurisdictions through the Vital Statistics Cooperative Program. https://wonder.cdc.gov/mcd-icd10.html. The query is described in data-raw/overdose.R in the package source.

Details

Deaths are those with an underlying cause of death coded as ICD-10 X40-X44 (accidental poisoning by drugs, medicaments and biological substances).

Following the CDC WONDER data use restrictions, death counts of 9 or fewer and the rates based on them are not included: these 20 cells are NA and flagged "suppressed". CDC WONDER does not report rates based on fewer than 20 deaths, which it considers unreliable; these 63 rates were computed from the deaths and population and flagged "unreliable".

References

Jalal H, Burke DS. Hexamaps for age-period-cohort data visualization and implementation in R. Epidemiology. 2020;31(6):e47-e49. doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000001236

Examples

hexamap(overdose_white_men, colorbar_range = c(0, 40),
        scale_units = "Deaths per 100,000",
        highlight = list(cohort = 1975))


table(overdose_white_men_long$flag)
#> 
#>   reliable unreliable suppressed 
#>       1037         63         20
